Date of filing of claim petition : 19.11.2018 Date of framing of issues : 05.08.2019 Date of concluding arguments : 19.02.2024 Date of decision : 15.03.2024 AWARD/JUDGMENT 1.

The claim for compensation raised in this claim petition is in respect of fatal injuries alleged to have been sustained by the deceased Sh. Babli Bhati in a motor accident that took place on 11.04.2018, at about 8 pm, on Noida-Surajpur Road, infront of Kanya Inter College, Bhangel,
District Gautam Budh Nagar, Noida, regarding which one FIR No.225/2018, under Sections 279/338/304-A IPC was registered at PS Phase-2, Noida, District Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P.

The vehicle involved in this case is a bus bearing registration No. DL-1PC-7176, which at the relevant time of accident was being owned by respondent no. 1 (R1), driven by respondent no. 2 (R2) and insured with respondent no. 3 (R3).
2. Succinctly put, facts of case as per claim petition are that the deceased was coming to his house from Noida on the motorcycle.

When he reached infront of Kanya Inter College, Bhangel on Noida Dadri Road, the offending vehicle bearing registration No. DL-1PC-7176, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at a high speed and in rash and negligent manner, came from behind and dashed against the back side of the motorcycle due to which he sustained grievous injuries.
It is further stated that the deceased was removed to Yatharth Wellness Hospital, Sector-108, Noida where he was declared brought dead by the doctors.
3. Respondent no. 1 and 2 have filed their joint reply to the claim petition wherein, it is stated that the alleged offending bus was falsely implicated in the present matter.

It is further stated that the offending vehicle was duly insured with M/s United India Insurance Company Ltd.
4.

Respondent no. 3/Insurance Company has filed its reply to the claim petition wherein it is stated that the offending vehicle was duly insured with them in the name of respondent no. 1 w.e.f.
06.11.2017 to 05.11.2018.
It is further stated that the alleged offending vehicle was falsely implicated in the present matter.
It is further stated that the respondent no. 2 was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.

5. On 05.08.2019, the following issues were framed by the Ld. Predecessor of this Court:-
1.

Whether Sh. Babli Bhati suffered fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 11.04.2018 at about 8 pm, on Noida- Surajpur Road, infront of Kanya Inter College, Bhangel, District Gautam Budh Nagar, Noida caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-1PC-7176 being driven by respondent No. 2, owned by respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No. 3 ? OPP.
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
3.Relief.

sentences.text: In support of their claim, the petitioner no. 1/wife of deceased has examined herself as PW1 and Sh. Kapil Kumar, an eye witness of accident as PW2.

The Tribunal heard the arguments advanced by Sh. Shrichand Chhawadi, Ld. Counsel for petitioners, Sh. Pradeep Kumar Singh, Ld. Counsel for R-1 and R-2 and Sh. Sudhindra Tripathi, Ld.
Counsel for R-3/Insurance Company and has carefully perused the entire record of the case as well as written submissions filed on behalf of parties.
The findings on the aforementioned issues are rendered hereinafter in the succeeding paragraphs.

1. Whether Sh. Babli Bhati suffered fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 11.04.2018 at about 8 pm, on Noida- Surajpur Road, infront of Kanya Inter College, Bhangel, District Gautam Budh Nagar, Noida caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-1PC-7176 being driven by respondent No. 2, owned by respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No. 3 ? OPP.
9.
Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
The first question that needs to be decided is whether the accident was caused by the vehicle bearing registration No. DL- 1PC-7176.

In order to prove the same, the petitioners have examined Sh. Kapil Kumar, an eye witness of the accident as PW2 who deposed that the deceased Babli was driving his motorcycle ahead of him in slow speed and on the correct side of the road.
All of a sudden, the offending bus bearing registration No. DL-1PC-7176 came from back side and dashed against the motorcycle of deceased due to which the deceased got injured.
He further deposed that the accident had occurred due to sole negligence of driver of the said bus.
10. During cross examination, he deposed that the deceased was riding ahead of him and was wearing helmet at the time of accident.
He denied that the deceased was driving his motorcycle at a high speed or in rash and negligent manner.
He further deposed that the helmet worn by the deceased broke after he fell down and it was lying on the site of accident.

He further deposed that the bus had come from behind and the offending bus also overtook his (PW2's) motorcycle as well,
but fortunately, it did not hit his motorcycle.
He further deposed that the FIR was lodged by his father after four days of the accident.
He further deposed that the FIR was registered late as they were in shock.
He further deposed that no call was made to PCR on the date of accident.
He further deposed that he did not note down the registration number of the bus, but he memorized it.
11. During the course of final arguments, Ld. Counsel for Insurance Company has drawn attention of this Tribunal towards the time since death mentioned in the postmortem report of deceased.

Since in the postmortem report of deceased, time since death was shown to be 3/4 days, therefore, the Insurance Company has examined one witness Dr. Sanjeev Kumar, Superintendent, Community Health Centre, Dadri, District Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P. as R3W1 who prepared the postmortem report of deceased.

He in his examination in chief has deposed that time since death as mentioned Sarita vs Delhi Transport Corporation on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103572481/
3 in the postmortem report means 18 hours meaning thereby that the death had occurred 18 hours (3/4th of day) prior to the conclusion of postmortem.

Considering the said version of doctor, I do not find any discrepancy in the record to raise any doubt in the genuineness of claim as the accident had occurred on 11.04.2018 and the postmortem was conducted on 12.04.2018 at 11.45 am, meaning thereby that the death had occurred in the evening hours of 11.04.2018 and further, as per FIR, the accident had occurred at 8 pm on 11.04.2018.
12.

Respondents have also taken the plea of false implication of offending vehicle by submitting that there is delay of 2 days in registration of FIR as the accident had taken place on 11.04.2018 whereas,
the FIR was registered on 13.04.2018.
13.

However, I do not find any force in the above contention raised by the Insurance Company regarding delay in lodging of FIR and in this regard, reliance is placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in case Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan, Civil Appeal No. 1926 of 2011 (arising out of S.L.P. (C)
No.11974 of 2008), decided on 18.02.2011,

entities.text: Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan, Civil Appeal No. 1926 of 2011
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
wherein it has been held as under :-
"......21.
The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases,
delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons."
14. As per chargesheet, the FIR was lodged at the instance of deceased's father who was a pillion rider on the motorcycle of PW2 and deceased was ahead of them on his separate motorcycle.
PW2 has been cited as primary witness and hence, his presence at the spot of accident cannot be doubted.

15. In cases National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287 and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors., 2014 (2) TAC 846 (Del.) decided by the Coordinate Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court, it was held that "......where the petitioners filed either the certified copies of the criminal record or the criminal record showing the completion of investigation by police or issuance of charge sheet under Section 279/304A IPC or the certified copy of FIR or the recovery of the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, then these documents are sufficient proof to reach to a conclusion that the driver was negligent particularly when there is no defence available from the side of driver."

sentences.text: It has been further observed that even when the accused were to be acquitted in the criminal case, the same may be of no effect on the assessment of the liability required in respect of motor accident cases by the Tribunal.

17. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.

Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the petitioners and the petitioners were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.

sentences.text: During cross examination, she deposed that her deceased husband had been working as a driver with M/s Kuldeep Tour & Travel for around six months prior to the accident.

As per her version, her deceased husband was having a driving license to drive a car and she has placed on record the copy of driving license of her deceased husband as Ex. PW1/R1/1.

It is pertinent to mention that as per appointment letter of deceased Ex. PW1/11, the deceased was appointed on the post of Supervisor on 01.01.2018 whereas, as per salary certificate Ex. PW1/12,
the deceased had worked with M/s Kuldeep Tour & Travels as Supervisor from 01.01.2017 to 11.04.2018.
Due to said discrepancies, the said documents do not seem genuine.

Even otherwise, the said documents have not been proved in accordance with law because neither the maker of said documents have been examined nor any other person from the office of employer was summoned with relevant record.
In absence of proof of income, the income of deceased has to be assessed as per Minimum Wages Act.
As per documents of education placed on record, it is established that the deceased was matriculate, though he had not passed his 12 th class.
In view thereof, the income of deceased is assessed as per the rates of minimum wages of a matriculate prevalent in U.P., which was Rs. 9,381/- per month (rounded off) at the time of accident.

25. In order to prove the age of deceased, PW1 has tendered on record copy of school transfer certificate of deceased as Ex. PW1/9 in which the date of birth of deceased has been recorded as 05.04.1993.
Hence, going by this documents, the age of deceased as on the date of accident i.e. on 11.04.2018 was around 25 years and 6 days.

In terms of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121,

14. As per chargesheet, the FIR was lodged at the instance of deceased's father who was a pillion rider on the motorcycle of PW2 and deceased was ahead of them on his separate motorcycle.

Deepak Goel and Ors., 2014 (2) TAC 846 (Del.) decided by the Coordinate Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court, it was held that "......where the petitioners filed either the certified copies of the criminal record or the criminal record showing the completion of investigation by police or issuance of charge sheet under Section 279/304A IPC or the certified copy of FIR or the recovery of the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, then these documents are sufficient proof to reach to a conclusion that the driver was negligent particularly when there is no defence available from the side of driver."
16. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Therefore, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against the respondent no.
2/driver in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
